title: 2.7.5 Individual PA Part 5: Write the Steps
description: One problem, pick one of three, write the JavaScript that solves it. Nested loop, branch, and break/continue required. AI-graded, summative.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Chapter 2 Individual PA Part 5: Write the Steps
aiGrader.prompt:
The student writes a complete JavaScript program (no functions, no arrays, no objects) that solves one of three problems. The program must contain: a nested loop, a branch (if/else if/else), a break or continue, and a try/catch guard. The student picks one of three problems from a menu. The program reads inputs from hardcoded constants (no user input), computes a result, and reports it with console.log. The AI grader evaluates:

1. Correctness: the program produces the correct output for the given test cases (provided in the rubric).
2. Structure: contains a nested loop (for/while inside for/while), an if/else if/else branch, at least one break or continue, and a try/catch around the risky input.
3. Documentation: header comment with Problem, Partners (N/A for individual), Date; UPPER_SNAKE_CASE const for the limit; camelCase variables; at least one template literal console.log; typeof reported for one value.
4. No functions, no arrays, no objects. Iteration only from counters or string indexing (word[i], word.length).

Rubric (20 points total):
- 8 pts: §2.1 branch (if/else if/else with && or ||)
- 12 pts: §2.4 loop and nesting (nested loop with break/continue inside)

The AI should award partial credit for partial structure (e.g., has nested loop but missing break).

rubric.title: Contains a nested loop
rubric.description: The program has a for/while loop inside another for/while loop. The outer loop iterates a range; the inner loop iterates a different range or walks a string.

rubric.title: Has an if/else if/else with && or ||
rubric.description: The program contains an if/else if/else chain with at least one compound condition using && or ||.

rubric.title: Uses break or continue inside the loop
rubric.description: The nested loop contains at least one break or continue that is not merely decorative (it affects control flow).
